Bein Hazmanim · Every morning

It's vacation. At 8:30 this morning, the beis medrash was full.

Boys from first grade through eighth pack the room every single day of bein hazmanim — to daven, eat breakfast, and learn. There's a program for girls too. It runs on breakfast, snacks, and a raffle table, and every bit of that is paid for by people who donate.

Where the money goes

Nothing here is optional

Take any one of these away and the program stops working the way it works.

Breakfast, every morning

A room full of kids, every morning of bein hazmanim. It's the first thing after davening, and the last thing anyone would give up.

Snacks at both recesses

Two recesses a day, every day of the zman. It adds up quietly.

Prizes for the raffle

Real prizes, every day, or the raffle stops meaning anything. This is what keeps attendance high.

Sefarim and supplies

Enough copies that no boy is sharing or sitting out.

Rebbeim to give the shiurim

Someone has to teach Navi at nine in the morning during their own bein hazmanim.

The girls' program

Smaller, and running on the same shoestring.

Why we're asking

None of this appears on its own

Breakfast every morning. Snacks at both recesses. Prizes worth winning. Enough sefarim for everyone. Rebbeim who give up their own bein hazmanim to teach. Every one of those things is there because somebody paid for it.

The learning happens either way — these boys keep showing up. The only question is whether the people running it are doing it with support behind them, or without.

That's the whole ask.
